reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the cited text supports it.

Section 14.3 supplies a genuine post-termination transition regime in PB's favour (assignment of the Trial Data Package and Product Filings, delivery of true and complete copies, PB-elected wind-down or transfer of control with continued conduct for a transition period, assignment of Clinical Trial/CRO/Vendor Agreements with cooperation on Site and Investigator notices), so the rule's 'missing/insert' trigger is not met.

Data return and deletion legs are covered: §11.1.1.4 vests sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package in PB on termination, and §10.3 requires return or destruction of Confidential Information at the Disclosing Party's direction with written certification by an authorized officer — matching the preferred position's certified-deletion element.

The failed deterministic check ('data return/transition present') is a phrasing artifact: the agreement uses pharma-specific language (Trial Data Package, Product Filings, transfer of Clinical Trials) rather than 'transition assistance' or 'machine-readable', so the regex miss does not undercut substantive compliance.

Shortfalls are correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged: the redacted ([***]) transition and delivery periods cannot be benchmarked against 6 months/30 days, and §14.3.4(ii) transition work is at PB's cost rather than at then-current rates — both minor sub-elements, and neither approaches walk-away (no immediate deletion or no-return risk).

Scope carve-out is handled correctly: the Program Transfer path under §3.20 / Exhibit O is properly assigned to change-of-control and remedies rules, avoiding double-flagging the same commercial term.
